::: {.why}
The model you wrote down last night has a semi-closed form, five interpretable parameters, and reproduces both the smile and its dynamics, which is why it is still the default after thirty years.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Name the five Heston parameters and say which feature of the surface each one controls.
- Calibrate Heston to your fitted surface and report the fit quality against local volatility's exact fit.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Calibrate Heston to your surface with QuantLib, which has the characteristic-function pricer implemented and tested. Report the calibrated parameters and the residuals across strikes and maturities. It will not fit exactly, unlike local volatility, and the pattern of residuals tells you where the model is too rigid.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Map parameters to features: long-run variance sets the level at long maturities, mean reversion speed sets how fast the term structure flattens, volatility of variance sets the curvature, and the correlation between the two Brownian motions sets the skew. Verify each by perturbing one parameter and replotting the surface.
:::
:::
